items.summary: WI level at the time of the auction: 4.622% High yield: 4.627% Tail: 0.5 basis points vs an average stop-through of 0.1 basis point Bid to cover: 2.53X vs the average of 2.64X Directs: 35.0% vs the average of 25.2% Indirects: 55.5% vs the average of 62.7% Dealers: 9.5% vs the average of 12.1% Auction grade: C− The auction was a little below average. The high yield came in 0.5 basis points above the when-issued level, and the bid to cover fell short of its average. Indirect bidders took a smaller share than usual, but direct bidders stepped up, taking 35.0% against an average of 25.2%. That helped keep the dealer takedown below average at 9.5%. The strong direct demand softened the result, but the tail and lighter overall bidding tipped the grade to a C−. This article was written by Greg Michalowski at investinglive.com.

items.title: Mahmood’s ICE-style immigration raid agency accused of ‘fishing expeditions’
items.summary: Exclusive: Almost two-thirds of visits lead to no arrests and nearly three-quarters are conducted without a warrant Shabana Mahmood’s ICE-style raid agency has been accused of engaging in “fishing expeditions” after figures disclosed that almost two-thirds of enforcement visits result in no arrests and nearly three-quarters are conducted without a warrant. The home secretary has hailed the expanded use of immigration enforcement teams, and claimed they will help to secure the UK’s borders by removing a key incentive for irregular migration. There were 23,538 immigration enforcement engagements such as workplace raids, home raids and spot checks in 2025 – or 60 a day. Of these, 15,578, or 66.1%, resulted in no arrests. Only 25.81% of visits where a premises was accessed used a warrant. Critics say this suggests the Home Office is launching “fishing expeditions” based on weak intelligence.

items.summary: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Renaud Foucart, Senior Lecturer at the Department of Economics ECARES at Lancaster University. France's 1.6% minimum-wage increase, in response to the countrywide protests, may offer a temporary reprieve from social unrest, but it does little to resolve the deeper political and institutional crisis confronting the country. According to Foucart, the central problem extends beyond declining purchasing power, fiscal constraints and the limitations of a minority government. It concerns a growing loss of faith in politics itself. “They are in the street because they don't believe politics can achieve anything,” Foucart argues, suggesting that the persistence of mass demonstrations ahead of the presidential election reflects profound disillusionment with the political system's capacity to deliver meaningful change.

items.title: Watching others pays off: Attentive macaques benefit from observing their group mates interacting
items.summary: Monkeys constantly observe and evaluate their social environment. It stands to reason that the social and mental abilities required to do so were favored by evolution. After all, these abilities should influence how an animal interacts with its conspecifics and, as a result, what social position it can attain within the group's hierarchy. Researchers from the DPZ and the University of Göttingen have now investigated whether this widely held assumption is correct by studying 46 wild male Assamese macaques in Thailand. The paper is published in the journal Current Biology.

For background, the Census Bureau’s monthly wholesale trade report, formally Monthly Wholesale Trade: Sales and Inventories, is released at 10 am ET about five to six weeks after the reference month ends. From Arctic landscapes to insect bodies, climate change is shifting the familiar colors of nature. Imagine the bright tones of coral under the sea. What do you see? What colors come to mind? Here's a look at BCCI's consent forms and rules for denying a trade and if a player can refuse to be traded to another team. No player in the Indian Premier League (IPL) can be traded without signing a BCCI consent form, and signing is entirely their choice. Trade talks between franchises cannot legally begin until that signed form reaches the BCCI. A player who consents cannot then pick his destination, as the selling franchise chooses the bid. Yes. The consent form sits at the centre of every IPL trade, and a player who declines to sign it cannot be moved, regardless of what the two franchises have agreed between themselves.

The government says pupils in Year 7 to 9 should have "richer, more engaging" learning than preparing for GCSEs. Secondary schools will be told not to teach GCSEs early as part of a major shake-up of how children in Years 7 to 9 are taught. The government plans to make Key Stage 3 a more distinct education phase, urging schools to focus less on exams and more on a "richer, more engaging" experience. The changes come in response to two reviews that found pupils were increasingly becoming disengaged in their early teenage years, affecting attendance and achievement, the Department for Education (DfE) said.

What a great play by Broncos safety Devon Key against the Panthers! Framesira/Shutterstock Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover One of Android's biggest learning curves is the way Google's operating system organizes apps. Unlike the iPhone, which puts all your apps on the home screen by default, Android tucks them into a dedicated window called an app drawer. The African National Congress, the party of late Nobel Prize winner Nelson Mandela, slumped to its worst-ever result in South Africa's municipal election. The voters blame the ANC for water and electricity shortages. Their closes rival, the Democratic Alliance (DA), won just under 25% of the vote. On 3rd-and-8 with 1:45 to play, Colts coach Shane Steichen called a pass instead of running clock before a field goal attempt. Why that was the right call Facing a third-and-8 at the Dallas 32-yard line with 1:45 left in Sunday's game, Steichen called a pass play in order to try to get the first down instead of handing it off in an effort to run clock. The Cowboys had just used their final timeout, Indianapolis had one down left at its disposal and Steichen knew Dallas would have enough time to drive into range for a game-tying field goal even if he ran off an extra 40 seconds in that situation.

If you've ever noticed plumes of heavy smoke emanating from an F1 car it might be something cold rather than something hot — here's how F1 teams use dry ice. Dry ice is carbon dioxide in solid form, sitting at a bone-chilling -109.3 degrees Fahrenheit. It doesn't melt into liquid like ice water — instead, it sublimates directly into gas, which makes it perfect for cooling high-performance components without leaving behind any moisture. That's key when you're dealing with tightly packaged electronics, batteries, and driver cockpits that are not water-friendly.

Habanero Pixel/Shutterstock Add Engadget on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover USB wouldn't be what it is today without Apple. The format predates the original iconic iMac — but Apple's gumdrop-shaped computer helped popularize it by ditching all the legacy connectors that had been haunting the industry. USB became so commonplace, in fact, that the push came back to bite the company, with European Union regulations forcing it to ditch Lightning ports on iPhones . An 8-year-old Haitian boy who lost Temporary Protected Status earlier this year was taken into federal custody during an immigration check-in. Med spas are raving about vitamin B12 shots as a pick-me-up. But do they actually make you feel more energized? I f you spend time on social media, you may have seen med spa owners and employees describing vitamin B12 shots as a pick-me-up . When they’re run down or facing a busy week, they say, a quick injection gets them through. Some med spas say many people feel an energy lift within a day or two and recommend a shot every few weeks. New figures suggest hazel dormice may be recovering after decades of decline, with warmer summers boosting survival. Dormouse numbers may be recovering in England and Wales after years of decline, offering a rare piece of good news for one of our best-loved mammals. The animal has disappeared from much of the countryside with conservationists warning of a long-term collapse in its population. However, new data suggests dormouse numbers increased between 2020-2025, a period that coincided with warmer springs and summers.

The education secretary says she is backing the inquiry to "get to the heart of the barriers holding children back". Action from "across society" is needed to help improve the educational outcomes of white working-class children, the co-chair of an independent inquiry looking into the issue has said. The inquiry's first report, published this summer , concluded that once-in-a-generation reforms were needed to fix a system "not serving the interests of white working-class children". The next phase will focus on early years children and teenagers aged 14 to 19, aiming for a stronger start at primary school and improving older students' routes through education into successful careers.

Here's everything to know about the DLS method and all the ways by which scores are calculated under the rain check. DLS calculates targets using resources, meaning overs remaining and wickets in hand together. The VJD method is the only serious modern rival, and it is used in Indian domestic cricket. Earlier systems failed because they ignored wickets, most notoriously at the 1992 World Cup. The Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method is the system cricket uses to reset a target when rain or any other interruption shortens a limited-overs match. It was devised by two English statisticians, Frank Duckworth and Tony Lewis, introduced in 1997 and adopted by the ICC two years later.

When a user chooses the “Yes, and don’t ask again” option to approve running a command, that choice gets stored as part of a rule in the local “.claude/settings.local.json” file on the user’s computer. That rule is sometimes coded as a pattern, but the command itself is often written to that settings file as is, including any sensitive information that may be embedded within it.

At 19, Blades Brown won the PGA Tour in Mexico after a massive comeback. This historic victory changes how the game is played and who wins. Most players would have folded with that kind of hole in the standings. Brown did not even blink. He closed with a nine-under 63 to force a playoff, according to the Associated Press. The final score was 23-under 265, which cleared a logjam of eight players who were all within a single stroke of one another. He bypassed college entirely to turn pro out of high school, a move that paid off instantly.
